details:
**Ems Dispatch**
An 1870 telegram reporting a meeting at the spa town of Ems between King Wilhelm I and French ambassador Count Vincent Benedetti. Bismarck edited it before releasing it to the press so that each side seemed to have insulted the other, provoking Napoleon III's France into declaring the Franco-Prussian War.

**"Blood and Iron" speech**
Bismarck's 1862 speech to the Prussian parliament's budget committee, arguing for higher military spending. He declared that "the great questions of the day" would be decided not by speeches and majority decisions, the mistake of 1848 and 1849, but by "iron and blood."

**Kulturkampf**
Bismarck's 1870s "culture struggle" against the influence of the Catholic Church in Germany, named by the scientist and politician Rudolf Virchow. It included expelling the Jesuits and was opposed by the Catholic Centre Party, whose leader Ludwig Windthorst was Bismarck's chief rival. It was wound down after Pope Pius IX died in 1878.

**May Laws**
Laws passed in 1873 by Prussian minister of culture Adalbert Falk as part of the Kulturkampf. They gave the state control over the training and appointment of Catholic clergy.

**"Iron Chancellor" and German unification**
Bismarck's nickname as minister-president of Prussia and then first chancellor of the German Empire. He unified Germany under King Wilhelm I, who was proclaimed German Emperor at Versailles in 1871, in a strategy of practical, power-based diplomacy known as realpolitik.

**Reinsurance Treaty**
A secret 1887 treaty between Germany and Russia in which each promised neutrality if the other went to war with a third power, with exceptions. Bismarck signed it after the League of the Three Emperors collapsed, and it was allowed to lapse after his dismissal.

**League of the Three Emperors (Dreikaiserbund)**
An alliance Bismarck formed between Germany, Austria-Hungary, and Russia, first in 1873 and again in 1881. It fell apart because of Austro-Russian rivalry in the Balkans.

**"Dropping the Pilot"**
An 1890 cartoon by John Tenniel in the British magazine Punch showing Bismarck, as a ship's pilot, walking down a ladder off a ship while Kaiser Wilhelm II watches from above. It satirizes Wilhelm II's dismissal of Bismarck, who was succeeded as chancellor by Leo von Caprivi.

**Seven Weeks' War and Schleswig-Holstein**
Bismarck fought Denmark in the 1864 Second Schleswig War over the duchies of Schleswig and Holstein, then divided them with Austria in the Gastein Convention. Disputes over that arrangement led to the 1866 Austro-Prussian (Seven Weeks') War, won at the Battle of Koniggratz and ended by the Peace of Nikolsburg and then the Peace of Prague.

**Welfare state (State Socialism)**
In the 1880s Bismarck created the first modern welfare state, including the 1883 Sickness Insurance Law, accident insurance, and old-age pensions. He meant these programs to weaken the Social Democrats and win over workers, and universal health insurance funded by workers and employers is still called the "Bismarck Model."

**Anti-Socialist Laws**
A series of laws starting in 1878 that banned socialist organizations and publications. Bismarck pushed them through after two assassination attempts on Wilhelm I, and they depended on support from conservative and liberal parties in the Reichstag.

**Ferdinand Cohen-Blind**
A student who tried to shoot Bismarck in Berlin in 1866. Bismarck survived as bullets glanced off his ribs, and Cohen-Blind killed himself in custody. Another would-be assassin, Eduard Kullmann, attacked Bismarck in 1874, which led him to intensify the Kulturkampf.

**Alvensleben Convention**
An 1863 agreement in which Prussia offered Russia help in suppressing the January Uprising in Poland. It won Bismarck the goodwill of Russian foreign minister Alexander Gorchakov.

**Congress of Berlin (1878)**
A conference hosted by Bismarck, as an "honest broker," that revised the Treaty of San Stefano after the Russo-Turkish War. Bismarck later warned that a great European war would start from "some damned foolish thing in the Balkans."

**Berlin Conference and German colonies**
The 1884–1885 conference Bismarck hosted to regulate European claims in Africa, which is linked to the "Scramble for Africa." Under Bismarck, Germany gained colonies such as Togoland and German New Guinea.
